bib.title: Measuring the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes

question: How many parameters does a neural network really need to solve a problem, measured as the smallest random-subspace dimension in which training reaches a solution?
hypothesis: Solutions are highly redundant, so the intrinsic dimension of a problem is far below the parameter count and changes little as the model grows.
contributions: Define intrinsic dimension of an objective landscape and estimate it by random subspace training
Measure d_int90 on MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet and RL tasks, enabling cross-domain difficulty comparison
Show d_int90 is nearly constant across FC models of very different size
Give an upper bound on minimum description length and a simple network compression scheme

method.summary: Train theta(D)=theta0(D)+P theta(d), with theta0 and the D x d projection P random and frozen, only theta(d) (init zero) trained. Sweep d, and report the smallest d at which performance reaches 90% of a directly trained baseline (d_int90).
method.task: measuring intrinsic dimension of supervised (MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet) and RL (CartPole, InvertedPendulum, Humanoid, Pong) objective landscapes

datasets.name: MNIST
datasets.preprocessing: shuffled-pixel variant: one random permutation applied to train and test; shuffled-label variant: labels randomised, training accuracy used

other.sweep: 20 FC nets, hidden layers {1..5} x width {50,100,200,400}; D varies 24.1x

models.name: FC / LeNet / ResNet-20 / SqueezeNet / ConvNet (Pong)
models.params: CIFAR FC 656,810; CIFAR LeNet 62,006; ResNet-20 280k; SqueezeNet 1,248,424; Pong ConvNet 1,005,974; Humanoid FC 166,673

training.objective: classification loss (supervised); DQN and Evolution Strategies (RL)
training.optimizer: SGD lr 0.1 and Adam lr 0.001 on MNIST FC (S5.4); RL ES uses Adam with beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999, eps 1e-7
training.lr: MNIST: SGD 0.1, Adam 0.001; ES Adam LR 3e-1 (InvertedPendulum), 3e-2 (Humanoid, Pong)
training.weight_decay: l2 penalty in ES: 1e-8 InvertedPendulum, 5e-3 Humanoid and Pong
training.regularisation: regularisation study (CIFAR FC L=2,W=200): l2 {1e-2,1e-3,5e-4,1e-4,1e-5,0}, dropout {0.5..0}
training.compute: ImageNet: each intrinsic dimension takes about 6 to 7 days on 4 GPUs
training.seeds: 3 runs per d on MNIST FC sweep (median), 50 bootstrap samples for variance; DQN at least 5 runs per d; most other experiments single run

other.projection: dense Gaussian (O(Dd)), very sparse (density 1/sqrt(D), Li et al 2006) for CIFAR-10, Fastfood transform for ImageNet and Pong; columns normalised to unit length
other.threshold: d_int90 = smallest d with performance >= 90% of best directly trained baseline; accuracy or reward (shifted min 0), not loss
other.RL performance: max-attained mean eval reward over iterations, averaged over 30 evaluations

metrics.name: d_int90
metrics.definition: smallest random-subspace dimension d whose performance is at least 90% of the directly trained baseline (validation accuracy, or total reward)

metrics.name: d_int100
metrics.definition: smallest d with performance statistically indistinguishable from baseline; found to vary widely, so not used

baselines: best directly trained model (global baseline of 100% accuracy for the MNIST FC grid, or per-model baseline)
eval.protocol: Sweep d upward, oversampling near the threshold; for MNIST FC grid take median of 3 runs per d and bootstrap std (50 samples); many other results are one-run.

results.claim: MNIST FC reaches 90% of baseline in a subspace of only about 750 dimensions out of 199,210
results.quote: we measure this network’s intrinsic dimension dint90 at about 750

results.claim: D varies 24.1x across 20 FC MNIST models but d_int90 varies only 1.33x
results.setup: 20 FC nets, depth 1-5, width 50-400, MNIST, global 100% baseline, 3 runs/d
results.note: With per-model baselines the factor is 1.42 (Fig S7).
results.quote: dint90 changes over this range by a factor of only 1.33

results.claim: LeNet on MNIST has d_int90 of 290, about 150x compression
results.quote: we ﬁnd dint90 = 290, or a compression rate of about 150× for this network

results.claim: Storing the 750-dim FC solution (seed + 750 floats) compresses 793kB to 3.2kB
results.setup: MNIST FC, 32-bit floats; subspace training gives no inference speedup
results.quote:
It leads to compression
(assuming 32-bit ﬂoats) by a factor of 260×

results.claim: Shuffling MNIST pixels leaves FC d_int90 at 750 but raises LeNet from 290 to 1400
results.quote: the intrinsic dimension of a convnet increases from 290 to 1400

results.claim: Memorising random labels on 50,000 MNIST examples needs d_int90 of 190,000 (3.8 floats per label)
results.setup: FC L=5 W=400, D=959,610, shuffled labels, training accuracy
results.quote:
requires a very high
dimension, dint90 = 190, 000, or 3.8 ﬂoats per memorized label

results.claim: CIFAR-10 is harder than MNIST: d_int90 9k (FC) and 2.9k (LeNet)
results.quote: 9k vs. 750 for FC and 2.9k vs. 290 for LeNet

results.claim: For >50% CIFAR-10 accuracy, FC, LeNet and ResNet need d_int90 about 9k, 2.9k, 1k
results.quote:
FC, LeNet and ResNet approximately
requires dint90 = 9k, 2.9k and 1k

results.claim: ImageNet SqueezeNet d_int90 not determined, only above 500k
results.setup: SqueezeNet D=1.24M, direct top-1 55.5%; at d=500k accuracy 34.34%; each d takes 6-7 days on 4 GPUs

results.claim: Inverted pendulum needs only 4 parameters; Humanoid 700; Pong 6k
results.note: Humanoid text says MNIST FC d_int90 is 650 in S6.2 and CIFAR convnet 2,500, versus 750 and 2.9k elsewhere.

results.claim: Pole-balancing DQN d_int90: CartPole 25, Pole 23, Cart 7
results.setup: DQN FC L=2 W=400, at least 5 runs per d, baseline 195.07

results.claim: Both local connectivity and weight tying lower d_int90: LeNet variants 290/600/425/2000 on MNIST
results.setup: LeNet, Untied, FCTied, FC-LeNet; MNIST threshold 90%

results.claim: Subspace training stabilises deep FC nets: direct training fails for depth > 5, subspace training stable at all depths
results.setup: FC on MNIST, SGD step 0.1, ReLU, He init, up to 10 layers; read from Fig S9

results.claim: Subspace training acts as implicit regulariser, beating direct training on test NLL when d is well chosen
results.setup: CIFAR-10 FC L=2 W=200, vs l2 and dropout; qualitative, Fig S15-S17

limits: Random linear subspaces only; the authors suggest better (non-linear or constructed) subspaces might contain solutions more likely.
The 90% threshold is a heuristic; d_int100 varies widely. Conclusions are said to hold qualitatively for other thresholds but this is not tested.
A constant intrinsic dimension was shown for one architecture/dataset family (MNIST FC), not claimed in general.
ImageNet d_int90 was not estimated (only >500k) due to time and memory.
Most numbers are single-run; only the MNIST FC sweep has 3 runs per d.
d_int is an upper bound on MDL; tightness unknown.
Paper studies training from random init on small vision/RL problems; it does not study pretrained or fine-tuned models, LoRA, layer selection, transformers or language models.
Subspace training does not speed up inference and is costlier per update (two modules).

terms.definition: the codimension of the solution set inside R^D: D = dint + s
intrinsic dimension of the 90% solution: solutions with performance at least 90% of the baseline
